Dick’s 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? , is one of the best and most influential sci-fi films of all time, but it took 35 years for it to get a direct sequel. Producers Broderick Johnson and Andrew Kosove acquired the rights to the franchise in 2011 through their production company, Alcon, and used them to develop Denis Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049 , which is set 30 years after the events of Scott’s film. Now, the timeline is moving forward again in Blade Runner 2099 , which premieres on Prime Video on Nov. 25, and the producers are already thinking about what’s next for the cyberpunk series after that.

items.title: AMD says it 'loves gamers' only weeks after proclaiming it is a datacenter-first company
items.summary:
AMD landed itself in hot water with gamers a couple of weeks back by saying the quiet part out loud: CEO Dr. Lisa Su announced that it was a "datacentre-first company" in a call with investors, who were likely to want to hear that sorta thing. Yet upon reaching gamers' ears, the news wasn't so well received.

Now, AMD Japan has tried to settle things down by proclaiming "AMD loves gamers."

(Image credit: AMD, X) To be fair, those two statements aren't mutually exclusive. AMD can be datacentre first, and absolutely is, and still claim to care about gaming. Though when supply for key components is tight and prices are rising, we're definitely looking for a little more than kind words at this time. 

What makes matters worse is that AMD Japan also added: "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else."

Now, that's a much tougher sell. 

In Q3, AMD made more than double the cash from its datacentre segment ($8.5 billion) than its client and gaming segment ($3.7 billion)—the latter includes various Ryzen, as well as Radeon, products. Pure gaming revenue was a mere $773 million, and dropping fast, whereas datacentre revenue was up 97%. 

So, from a purely business perspective, AMD is undoubtedly all in on datacentres. I don't like to admit it, but it makes sense for a company owned by shareholders to go after the biggest growth market. But all the more reason not to claim an undying love for gamers—it just doesn't pass muster.

There's bad news for any GTA 6 fans still hoping for a 60fps option on PlayStation 5 Pro. 

While Sony's beefier PS5 is arguably the most powerful console on the market today, even it is unable to run Rockstar's new masterpiece at 60fps. That's according to the game's technology production director Marc Chambers, who admitted that the PS5 Pro could only do so much.

Somewhat controversially, GTA 6 targets 30fps across all of its supported console platforms, with the same rate on everything from the under-powered Xbox Series S all the way up to PS5 Pro.

Naturally, there are other differences — and the game's PS5 Pro version has a few extra bells and whistles. But anyone expecting a better frame rate will need to temper their expectations — at least, perhaps, until the game's PC version arrives.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," Chambers told Kotaku .

That said, PS5 Pro still offers other improvements, he continued. "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination," Chambers noted. "On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). items.title: GTA 6 Uses FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S to Upscale From 720p to 1080p
items.summary:
GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off. 

Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, according to an interview with Wccftech . That would make GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox, and it's probably what made the game possible on the budget console. 

I've already spent a bit of time with the Xbox Series S version of GTA 6, and while it does look a bit rough around the edges (literally), it looks better than I was expecting. Objects in the game are still incredibly detailed, but the edges of some objects – particularly distant buildings and hair – have a noticeable sheen of aliasing around them. But that lower resolution rendering is what lets the game mostly sit at around 30 fps (though I did notice a couple drops down to the mid-20s.)

According to the interview, though, the Xbox Series S is the only version of the game that's running on FSR 4. Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game are instead using Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro is using PSSR 2.0. It shouldn't be surprising either, that the Xbox Series S is also running at the lowest input resolution out of all of the consoles at 720p, compared to 1440p on all of the other consoles. 

When Wccftech asked Rockstar about the reasons it picked each…
items.t: GTA 6 Uses FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S to Upscale From 720p to 1080p

items.title: GTA 6 Xbox Series S Performance: How Does the Weakest Console Handle the Biggest Game of All Time?
items.summary:
GTA 6 is finally here , and one of the biggest questions heading up to launch is how well the Xbox Series S would handle the game – well, I've finally had the chance to play the game on the tiny Xbox. 

Rockstar announced a couple weeks ago that all versions of GTA 6 would be 'targeting' 30 fps , and while it's disappointing that even the PS5 Pro won't be able to hit 60 fps, that performance is about what I expected from the Xbox Series S. And while I wait for my framerate analysis to stop running on my first clip of the game, the Xbox Series S version actually seems pretty decent, all things considered. 

The Xbox Series S obviously doesn't have the same graphics treats that the PS5 Pro version of the game has, but even without the ray traced shadows and the PSSR, the game holds up well on the 1440p machine. Character models are still extremely detailed, and even has some decent subsurface scattering and the environments are incredibly beautiful, no doubt learning from Rockstar's time with Red Dead Redemption 2. 

But where the Xbox Series S falls short is in the finer details. The edge of nearly every surface is aliased, almost looking like there's a border of static around every character and building, particularly around people's hair. There's also an early scene on a boat, where Jason's face is noticeably soft until it zooms closer in, no doubt to save on some GPU resources. But, GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S is using FSR 4 to upscale from 720p up to 1080p, so some softness is to be expected.

items.title: GTA 6 is Now The Joint-Highest Rated Game of All Time
items.summary:
GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews in the past hour. 

Rockstar's masterpiece currently sits with an all-time best score of 99 on Metacritic , an honor shared only with Nintendo's original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time release back in 1997 on N64, almost 30 years ago. No other game since has managed such a feat. (The new version of Ocarina for Switch 2 managed a paltry score of just 96.)

While both the N64 version of Ocarina and GTA 6 share a 99 average, GTA 6 has impressively managed to pull this off with more than six times' the number of reviews — over 120 at the time of writing, with over 100 of those listed with a perfect score. And while it's possible GTA 6's ranking could still slip down a point as more reviews are published, it would still be the best-rated game in nearly three decades.

Few others titles released in the recent memory have come anywhere close to this — though if you head back to the last console generation, Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Super Mario Odyssey both managed a 97 average, a standing they share with Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2.

IGN's GTA 6 review is of course now live, and also returned a perfect 10/10 score. We described it as "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered," as well as "unprecedented, unbelievable and unmissable."

items.summary:
After Jensen Huang's departure from the company last week, Nvidia is now on the hunt for its next permanent CEO. Speaking in the Q&A section of Nvidia's Q3 2027 earnings call , board chair Harvey Jones says the directors are taking the search "very seriously."

"We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates" says Jones. "The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully."

Jones also says the company "won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person," but Amazon boss Jeff Bezos seems to think that hiring outside of Nvidia would be a mistake. 

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," says Bezos, speaking at the Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday (via Yahoo Finance ). "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding, and so I would always think that's a last resort."

Nvidia is currently being helmed by CFO Collette Kress as an interim chief, while recent reports have suggested that Huang may make a potential return to the company.

items.title: GTA 6 honor system: how your 'criminal profile' works
items.summary:
GTA 6 's criminal profiles (plural, because Jason and Lucia each have their own criminal profile) tracks how you treat other people in the world, reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. How violent you are, how lethal you are in your encounters, and how you treat people and animals in the world will all affect your rating.

Criminal Profile levels 

(Image credit: Rockstar) There are five levels for Jason and Lucia's criminal profile, represented by "face with horns" emoji-style icons that are shown on your screen:

Professional (yellow icon) Hardened (orange icon) Violent (purple icon) Psycho (light gray icon) Irredeemable (dark gray icon) How Criminal Profiles work 

(Image credit: Rockstar) Your criminal profile is almost entirely dependent on how often you kill people . Try to incapacitate enemies, or wound them instead of killing them, and don't kill too many police or civilians, and you'll wind up with a Professional or Hardened profile. If you're violent for no reason, kill a lot of cops and civilians, and kill pets or defenseless animals, you'll gain a Violent, Psycho, or Irredeemable profile.

items.title: How GTA 6 Came Together at Rockstar North
items.summary:
Current Rockstar North Co-Studio Head and Head of Development Rob Nelson seems relaxed for a man in Rockstar North’s bridge, essentially moments from steering what may well be the most anticipated entertainment product launch of all time into port — after 13 long years, no less.

What’s perhaps more interesting, however, is how even Nelson is quite happy to concede that not even he quite knows how a game as fundamentally huge and absolutely astonishing as GTA 6 has come together so magically. Money and talent is only a part of the answer; the rest is perhaps a little more nebulous.

“I think it takes a lot of obstinance, really,” explains Nelson. “Just a sort of stubborn persistence in pursuit of the same thing for a long time, and a team that’s been together for a really long time. Now a really, really long time.

“And the answer is I don’t know. I mean, I only know my part of it, which is a part of it. And the stuff that [co-studio head] Aaron [Garbutt] does, and the stuff that [director of technology] Phil [Hooker] does, and the stuff that the programming team does, I don’t know. They just do it and we sort of build it up in layers.”

Nelson explains that Hooker sent an update through to the team very recently that showcased the progress of missions, areas, and features in the game over the last few years, and says it was “shocking to see how far it’s come.”

“Well, unfortunately, lots of people saw it in the hack that we had a few years ago — where [the game] was,” he says. “And I think in development you forget that. You forget the doldrums that you go through and you…

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Review
items.summary:
During my first dozen-or-so hours with Grand Theft Auto 6, I fixed my leaky roof, collected some rum from a shady liquor store, played way too many games of pool, read a book about World War 2 soldiers with a penchant for teabagging, and caught a lot of fish. On the more ridiculous end of the spectrum, I also temporarily… borrowed a luxury yacht called Party on the Poop Deck before running it aground and drinking its owner’s beer, slapped the crap out of a bloke who cursed at me, found a finger in my horniest neighbour’s plumbing, threatened an alligator wearing a hat, and got mugged by a drunk sea captain with a harpoon gun – before stealing his weapon while he peed in a garden. 

Over 100 hours later, I’ve now completely lost track of all the things I’ve seen and done within GTA 6’s astounding open world – and I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it. While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit – despite hitting the credits after almost 120 hours of hijinks. Frankly, I’ve never played anything that’s hit quite like GTA 6 – and right now I have zero plans to stop playing it.

Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are an interesting pair of playable characters, and unlike any leads that have come before them in the series. Their motivations and goals are very different from the main characters of previous GTA games, and their priority is really about escape rather than revenge or empire…
items.t: Grand Theft Auto 6 Review

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Story Missions — Here’s Why
items.summary:
Think you’ll want to replay some of GTA 6 ’s most exciting missions? Well, you won’t be able to simply do that from any of its menus.

Now, not every game allows you to do this, so Rockstar’s latest is by no means an outlier in this regard, but seeing as practically every one of the studio’s games since The Ballad of Gay Tony expansion for GTA 4 has allowed you to do so, it is a little surprising.

GTA 6 is a little different from other games in the series, though. Its story flows and branches in small and big ways in a fluid manner not quite seen in any of the developer’s other open worlds. I’ve only completed one full playthrough myself, but can confirm that whole missions can play out differently based on decisions you didn’t even necessarily know you were making hours earlier. For example, one of GTA 6’s best missions, a daring high-stakes heist, can go relatively smoothly or turn out to be a much messier operation. 

What’s most exciting is that, now knowing this, I’m left wondering how many new things I’ll see in the second playthrough I’ve just started, as much as I am looking forward to replaying the missions I can’t easily access. The decision by Rockstar not to include the option to revisit them at launch may well prove controversial, and who knows if it will be added post-launch, but I can see the argument as to why they’ve decided to do it this way.

items.title: GTA 6 Photo Mode Confirmed at Launch
items.summary:
GTA 6 is a gorgeous-looking game, so naturally, you’ll feel the urge to pause regularly to take it all in. Thankfully, Rockstar knows this and has included a full-fledged photo mode at launch.

The developer is no stranger to such a concept, with GTA 5 including a whole movie director mode, and Red Dead Redemption 2 eventually gaining a photo mode alongside its PC launch. It’s a pleasant surprise, then, that it's here from the get-go with GTA 6.

It took 70 hours to complete my first playthrough of Jason and Lucia’s story, but I’d be lying if I said a couple of those hours weren’t spent messing around taking pictures when the mood struck me. Sometimes the light bounces perfectly off those waters off Ocean Beach, and you just can’t help but capture the moment.

The photo studio, found by pausing the game and hitting the square button on PS5/X button on Xbox, is impressively well-equipped, too. With aspect ratios, aperture, and depth of field all available to play with when it comes to the camera itself, a variety of different lighting from spotlights to floodlights to softboxes all available to insert into scenes, and a range of post-processing tools including a variety of filters, it’s a relatively impressive suite that I’ve enjoyed playing around with.

That being said, there are a few little things here and there that I’d love to see Rockstar introduce in future updates. Perhaps the primary one of those is the ability to reposition Jason and Lucia into new poses and change their facial expressions. Sometimes you just get that perfect background scenery, but unfortunately…

items.title: GTA 6 Switches Sprint to L3, Saving Thumbs Globally
items.summary:
Ever since Grand Theft Auto made the switch to 3D space with 2001’s GTA 3 , players have had to make use of the X button on PlayStation or the A button on Xbox to sprint. Up until San Andreas , holding down the relevant face button would trigger sprint, but CJ’s story changed that to just meaning “run”, with a repeated tap introduced for a full-fledged sprint. It’s been that way ever since with Rockstar’s games, including most recently 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2 , leaving sore thumbs globally at the end of long chase sequences.

Well now, with GTA 6 , everything has changed.

Finally, Rockstar’s return to Vice City changes the default sprint button to a press of the left analog stick, with a click of L3 making both Jason and Lucia sprint easily. You get the sense that the developer knows what a big deal this is, too, with one of the very first screens you see when first booting up GTA 6 being a warning about this change, alongside a message letting you know you can revert back to a more classic control scheme if you like.

Interestingly, in a fun little easter egg of sorts, there is one instance you’ll have to run where the traditional button mapping does return. In a nod to the series’ past, if you use a treadmill at one of the map’s several gyms, the minigame asks you to repeatedly press down the X/A button at the correct rhythm to score as high as possible. So, if you fancy getting either of the protagonists in great shape, you’ll also be giving your thumb a workout at the same time.

items.title: 100 hours with GTA 6: A sprawling adventure that will be so much better on PC
items.summary:
This isn't a review.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is not on PC so I can't review it. But somehow I, a member of PC Gamer, got access to GTA 6 before it launched. For the past two weeks I've secretly sunk approximately 100 hours in it (on something called a PlayStation 5) and now, finally, I can talk about it. What a relief. 

So this isn't a review, but I can give a verdict of sorts:

It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC. 

The world is even bigger than I expected 

(Image credit: Rockstar) I guess I shouldn't be surprised by just how massive and detailed the world is. It's Rockstar: huge open worlds is what they do, and they've had a decade to do it. But I was stunned when I started playing, and a hundred hours later, I'm honestly still pretty stunned. Rockstar said GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's map, but it feels twice as big as "twice as big" should feel. It's enormous. 

I'm constantly impressed by the macro and micro of it all. I can step back and take in the sheer size and scale of Leonida: the archipelago representing the Florida keys to the south, the vast wetlands standing in for the Everglades, the dense neighborhoods and shining skyscrapers of Vice City, the miles of beaches and forests and industrial areas and state parks. And I can zoom in and admire the tiny details: the carefully placed clutter and photos and belongings in a stranger's apartment, the accurate mating rituals of two great blue herons in the wild, or the font choice on a printout pinned to the wall of an office cubicle instructing employees on…

Here's a terrifying reminder that the cold hand of Death is on my shoulder: I'm pretty sure I first played Black Mesa back in 2012, at the tender age of 19. In the intervening 14 years, the fan-made Half-Life 1 remake has walked quite the road, including getting Valve's official blessing to sell itself—for money!—on Steam in 2015.

And they're still going, the mad lads. Just yesterday, Black Mesa got a hefty major update "featuring visual upgrades, engine optimizations, and a complete interface overhaul". It's called the Anomalous Improvements Update and it's a real humdinger.

The biggest improvement—if you are me, a man who tries to play basically everything on his Steam Deck these days—is the Steam Deck verification and much-improved controller support. The game will now recognise and let you use a gamepad right from the jump, rather than forcing you to faff around in settings, and generally seems like a rather seamless delight on Deck in the little bit of time I've mucked about with it.

Black Mesa's also been optimised "to deliver significantly better performance across the entire game". By way of evidence, the devs show a side-by-side of Gordon Freeman hanging out in Xen. Pre-update, he gets ~130 fps. Post-update, he gets ~170. Now, admittedly, both of these framerates fall into a category I like to call "absolutely fine", but it's always nice to squeeze a little more juice out of a game.

items.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
items.summary:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .
items.t: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

items.title: Civilization dev Firaxis reportedly lays off a third of its staff, studio head departs
items.summary:
A Bloomberg report says Civilization studio Firaxis has laid off roughly 60 people, representing about one-third of its total headcount. Heather Hazen, who took over as studio head in 2023 after more than 25 years with Firaxis, is also leaving.

A 2K Games spokesperson didn't comment on the reported number of employees let go, but confirmed that layoffs had occurred in a statement provided to PC Gamer. "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," the rep said.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

The rep also confirmed that Hazen has stepped down as Firaxis studio head: "With the studio entering this reset, she feels this is the right, deliberate moment to hand over the reins to ensure the next studio leader has full ownership of this new era from the start."

Firaxis has enjoyed great success as the developer of the Civilization and XCOM games, but it's struggled in recent years. Marvel's Midnight Suns was critically acclaimed but sales were middling, while Civilization 7 was just middling overall: Despite a raft of updates and changes since its 2025 release, its user rating on Steam remains stubbornly "mixed" while player numbers are still well behind that of Civilization 6.…

items.title: Jensen Huang says he would come back as Nvidia's CEO if America needs him – a technique I now intend to use at my next job interview
items.summary:
Jensen Huang says he would be honoured to return to his role as Nvidia's CEO should the company's board want him. The problem for Huang is, the board don't seem to. 

In a statement sent to CNN , among others, Huang lays out his now clear-as-day faults and makes a pitch for his old job back.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang says.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

President Donald Trump and a cohort of silicon valley execs have previously backed the Nvidia co-founder, even if Trump did wobble his way over to backing ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for a day. A heap of signatures were also added to a #bringjensenback petition , supposedly including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Sweeney has barely come up for air he's so wound up about Huang's resignation. 

Yet all these big names won't mean much if Huang can't convince the company's board of directors.

Last we heard, Nvidia's board was intent on moving past Huang . That's according to someone close to the matter speaking to CNBC . There are also a lot of things hanging over Huang at the moment, including an internal investigation at Nvidia, a couple of chats with Congress , an ongoing investigation into Nvidia's customer, Megaspeed , and any potential share price shock as markets would react to the news.

items.title: 'I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM' says Sam Altman, weeks after seeming to say the opposite
items.summary:
Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor , he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge ).

Altman says, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great."

So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". He argues that the optimal way to use memory is to share it (in this case, he seems to be referring to the use of AI in home rigs), and "have it working 100% of the time. Rather than, like, sometimes off in someone's Edge device."

So I guess if we all share RAM, we get more at the end of the day. I'll wait for OpenAI to share its memory with me, and then I might do the same. 

Altman points out that he got in more trouble a few years ago for saying there would be "a huge squeeze on memory". He then notes that many didn't believe it would be such a worry, and "we have seen DRAM prices, I don't know exactly, but maybe they went up like 5x, 7x or something like that. I think it would be much better if the world just had a lot of memory."

(Image credit: Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg via Getty Images) AI server…

items.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI
items.summary:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

The manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

items.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
items.summary:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics , together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus . Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.
items.t: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
items.summary: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country.

items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.summary:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.
items.t: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

items.title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes
items.summary:
Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".
items.t: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes
